title: Build questions to need the text
statement: Make a question need its text by how the text and the item format are built, not by filtering, patching or regenerating questions afterwards.
example: Built to need the text, 60% of items survived the without-text check, against 6% of encyclopedic clones.
detail: In the Grade 5 course, items generated construction-first survived the anti-leak gate at 60% against 6% for encyclopedic clones, and raw generated banks leaked ~94% blind (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`, lines 21-23). On the same encyclopedic passages, a cross-family run found leak rates of MCQ 99.5% and MSQ 100% against hot-text 1.67% and 0% for sequence, match and two-part evidence items, and conversion lanes showed the leaky formats could be redesigned into passage dependence (choice 142/234 converted; hot-text 90/117) (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g5-reading/brainlifts/v0.6.qmd`, lines 23-29). Questions built to need their text survive the without-text check far more often.
against: The 0% for ordering items came from a gate that scored one seeded shuffle per item, and a re-probe under four shuffles later decertified 65 of 118 (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/courses/g5-reading/analysis/seq-reprobe-2026-07-07/README.md`); the spec calls the 60% and 6% a historical basis for pricing and design, not current readiness (`grade3-reading/ti-courseplans/docs/practice-layer-spec.md`, line 20). A change of format alone did not fix it: a later check by two model families found 94.6% of 353 items in the formats thought safe still leaked, confirming that a leak-resistant format is not the same as a low leak rate (`grade3-reading/artifacts/g5-merged-course/a2-cross-family-regate.md`, line 21).

evidence.quote: construction-first generation survived the anti-leak gate at 60% vs 6% for encyclopedic clones
different blind-solve leak rates by question *format*: MCQ 99.5%, MSQ 100% — hot-text 1.67%, > sequence 0%, match 0%, EBSR 0% (cross-family run, 2026-06-23/24).
**MCQ/MSQ format does not force reading; hot-text, sequence and match do.**
leaky-by-default formats convert under per-item redesign.
Regen pilot (Wave 3) showed 9.5pt improvement in MCQ leak (99.5% → 90.0%) but leak remained
**Fix verdict:** NOT fixable with option-length patches. Requires passage strategy redesign.
- Skeleton redesign (V2) resolves the regen problem by eliminating MCQ/MSQ from the build and substituting passage-dependent formats with sufficient pool depth.
First, prefer the resistant formats for anything carrying weight: hot text, match, sequence and short constructed response, which have no options to guess between.
The one converting rewrite was a **text_entry item whose answer is a verbatim passage phrase**
Verbatim passage-phrase text-entry — answer is a verbatim passage phrase (the G8-POC's one converting rewrite; strongest passage-binding).
Mastery gate hardened live, 84.2% → 64.0% blind-solvable after 47 hardened items deployed

the root cause is not item quality — it is passage design. Encyclopedic passages make MCQ/MSQ/EBSR answerable without reading, at rates that regeneration alone cannot fix without rewriting the passage corpus.
Fact-disjointness is a design input, not a red-team afterthought
